findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — Server schema only validates each guest is an email but does not dedupe/reject duplicate emails within the guests array, while the client-side duplicate zod schema in AddGuestsDialog.tsx explicitly rejects duplicates via a Set-size refine; the handler's uniqueGuests filter (addGuests.handler.ts:56-60) only excludes emails already on the booking, not duplicates within the same input array, so calling the API directly (or via any future client) with `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` creates two duplicate attendee rows, silently diverging from the validation the UI promises

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26 — Guest-email validation schema is duplicated between this client component (with a uniqueness `.refine`) and packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts (no uniqueness check), so the two can silently drift out of sync with no shared source of truth

packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:12 — MultiEmail was added to the shared packages/ui package but currently has exactly one consumer (AddGuestsDialog.tsx), a premature generalization into a shared component before a second use case exists

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/_router.tsx:83 — The "// Unreachable code but required for type safety" defensive re-check after the dynamic import is copy-pasted boilerplate duplicated per-handler (also present for editLocation, confirm, etc.), so it is a pre-existing repo-wide pattern rather than complexity newly introduced by this PR, but it is dead code repeated at every call site instead of being centralized once

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — Guest attendee rows are created via prisma.booking.update/createMany before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees runs, with no transaction or compensating rollback, so if the calendar update throws the new attendees remain persisted in the DB while the calendar/video event never reflects them, leaving a permanent inconsistent state

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26 — Guest-email validation schema is duplicated between this client component (with a uniqueness `.refine`) and packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts (no uniqueness check), so the two can silently drift out of sync with no shared source of truth

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two separate validation schemas: in `apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx` a local `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` adds a uniqueness `.refine`, while the server-side `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts` only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness rule. This is a diff-grounded maintainability/consistency issue because client and server validation can diverge (and already do) without a shared source of truth.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — Guest attendee rows are created via prisma.booking.update/createMany before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees runs, with no transaction or compensating rollback, so if the calendar update throws the new attendees remain persisted in the DB while the calendar/video event never reflects them, leaving a permanent inconsistent state

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the code persists new attendees first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no surrounding transaction and no compensating rollback. Since `updateCalendarAttendees` is not wrapped in a try/catch, if it throws (e.g., external calendar API failure), the mutation will error while the DB remains updated with the new attendees, leaving the booking’s persisted attendee list out of sync with the calendar event state.
